frames.heading: How and why: proximate and ultimate

lines.say: Every behaviour can be explained two ways. Proximate means process: how it happens.
Ultimate means use: why it evolved, and how it helps fitness.
A bird sings in spring. Longer days change its hormones. That's proximate.

draw.alt: Bird song explained by proximate and ultimate causes

lines.say: Singing wins mates and territory. That's ultimate. A full answer needs both.
Innate behaviour is done right the first time, with no experience.
A goose rolls an egg back, and finishes the move even if the egg is taken.
Habituation: birds learn to ignore a scarecrow.
Imprinting: goslings follow the first moving thing they see.
Operant conditioning: a predator gets sick from a bright insect, and avoids that colour.
Most behaviour mixes genes and environment. It's a continuum.
Profitability is bang for your buck: energy divided by handling time.
A large crab gives 600 joules in 20 seconds. That's 30 joules per second.
A small crab gives 150 in 10 seconds. That's only 15.
If large crabs take 30 seconds to find, the rate is 600 over 50. Just 12.

draw.alt: Rate from large crabs only, 12, is below small crab profitability 15

lines.say: Fifteen beats twelve, so eat small crabs too. It depends on how common the best prey is.
Marginal value theorem: leave a patch when it's no better than average.
Signals can be visual, acoustic, chemical or tactile.
A honeybee waggle dance shows food direction by angle, and distance by duration.
Costly signals tend to be honest. Only fit animals can afford them.
Eggs are big and few, sperm small and many. Females are often the limiting resource.
Males compete, females choose. That's sexual selection, which explains the lyrebird's tail.
Monogamy, polygyny, polyandry or promiscuity. Care depends on certainty of paternity.
Altruism lowers your fitness but raises another's. Relatives share genes, though.
Hamilton's rule: help when relatedness times benefit is greater than cost.
A young bird can breed alone and raise one, or help raise 3 extra full siblings.
0.5 times 3 is 1.5. That beats 1, so helping wins.

draw.alt: Benefit to kin 1.5 versus cost 1; for half-siblings 0.75

lines.say: For half siblings, r is 0.25. Then r B is only 0.75, so breed alone.
Haplodiploid bee sisters share 0.75. Non-relatives need reciprocal altruism.
Territories limit how many animals can breed. That regulates population size.
Prey avoid risky areas. That's a landscape of fear.

draw.alt: Dingo suppresses foxes and cats, helping small native mammals

lines.say: Research suggests dingoes may suppress foxes and cats, helping small native mammals.
Selection acts on individuals and genes. Never for the good of the species.
